title: Do We Cut the Shot with the Boots?
brief: The Itch Be Gone ad goes live tomorrow. HQ just axed the studio shoot and wants a product shot where the rain boots used to be.

lines.text: Searches for Itch Be Gone are down. HQ wants the tube on screen in the first second.
The studio shoot's gone, too. They need a cut by noon or they'll run last year's.
I remember those boots you drew. Will people know where to buy the stuff, though?
I'll go take a look. The store might have the shot we're missing.
Try the corner store on Songshou Road. While you're there, ask who's been buying lately.

steps.hint: 去松壽路的巷口超商問問：最近誰在買腳癢退散？

lines.text: A delivery guy came in this morning, stood by that red chair, and poured water out of his rain boots.
Did he grab the cream right after that?
He stuffed his wet socks into one of our plastic bags first. Then he came over and asked where we kept the cream.
We could keep the bit where he ties the bag. Which shelf is it on? Mind if I get a shot?
Second shelf to the right of the register. You can shoot the shelf, just keep customers' faces out of frame.

steps.prompt: You've got a shelf photo on your phone and time to send one cut before lunch. What do you do?

options.text: Cut a six-second sales spot from the existing product shots and show where to find it by the register.
options.feedback: The spot makes the next day's slot. The clerk says someone came in with the ad on their phone and bought a tube on the spot. Then HQ hears from other stores: they don't stock it by the register.
options.insight: The 2019 yearbook notes that E.SUN Bank used data-driven attribution and found that non-brand keywords accounted for nearly 60% of conversion credit. After adjustments, its conversion rate rose 42%.

options.text: Make two storyboard cuts on your phone and ask Kai to show them to a few people and see if they can point out where the cream is stocked.
options.feedback: A few people who see the boots-first cut recognize the box but miss where the register is. You send HQ the results and both cuts, and they give you half a day to pick up a shelf shot.
options.insight: The 2019 yearbook points out that data only covers what gets recorded. Sample surveys, interviews at stores, and small data can help uncover clues it misses.

options.text: Borrow the store for the last half hour before closing and shoot a short film following a delivery rider from emptying his boots to buying the cream.
options.feedback: You kneel in the doorway to reshoot the water pouring out, then edit back at the office until the last train's gone. The film goes up a day late, but someone in the comments recognizes their own kind of rain boots and tags the brand for a coworker to see.
options.insight: The 2019 yearbook discusses weaving brands into stories as a way to reach people who skip or block ads. It also stresses that the placement has to serve the story.
